claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy is homogeneous and single-phase.
The initial alloy has a uniform elemental distribution.
The constituent elements of HfNbTaTiZr have sufficiently different thermal expansion rates to generate internal thermal stresses.
Internal stresses arising from differential thermal expansion drive local compositional segregation at elevated temperatures.
Thermal cycling or aging produces nano-scale compositionally segregated clusters in HfNbTaTiZr.
The nano-scale clusters impede dislocation motion.
Cluster-mediated dislocation pinning reduces the high-temperature creep rate.
Cluster-mediated dislocation pinning increases microhardness after cold rolling.
Nano-scale compositional clusters modify the temperature dependence of the elastic moduli.
Localized thermal-expansion mismatch associated with segregated regions influences stress-strain and thermoelastic behavior.
The proposed segregation mechanism is primarily active between 600 °C and 1250 °C.
Below 600 °C, limited diffusion suppresses segregation effects.
Thermally cycled specimens will exhibit more nano-scale compositional heterogeneity than the untreated baseline.
Thermally cycled specimens will have lower creep rates at 1250 °C than the untreated baseline.
After equivalent cold rolling, thermally treated specimens will have greater microhardness than the untreated baseline.
Thermally treated specimens will show a different elastic-modulus response over 293–1100 K than the untreated baseline.
